page.layout: One page of text in a single column, no marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. Catchword at lower right.

p.i: Cumq; diu pauit cuculum officiosa uoracem, Nec tamen ingluuiem iam saturare potest: Tum sibi seruatæ soluens mala præmia uitæ, Nutricem cuculus deuorat ore suam, &c.

main_text.p: Sedenim huic nostro instituto aliud eiusdem uiri Epigramma, de Naui Christi, quæ est Ecclesia Dei, pulcrè quadrat.

p.i: Auricomum uellus postquam transuexit Iason In patriam, sperans debita regna sibi: Oppressit dominum nauis de culmine lapsa, Sed qua desessus iam cubat ipse domi. Non te Christe tamen tua, quam regis, opprimet Ar- Quamuis & rimis est lacerata suis. (go, Tunc quoq; cum fluctus ciet imo ex gurgite Orion, Et rapidi uenti prælia sæua mouent: Quassatam in medio pelago tua dextera seruat, Et uere es nautis anchora sacra tuis. O uiua effigies æterni luxq; Parentis, Defendas cœtus optime Christe tuos: Qui tua non ficta discunt oracula mente, Aq; tuo poscunt Numine semper opem.

main_text.p: Hactenus primā Psalmi partem, prolixè traditam, persecuti sumus. Eam si quis centro & spacio breuiter circumscri bere uolet, adducat hæc uerba è Psalmo 90. v.16. Appareat erga seruos tuos opus tuum,& gloria tua filijs eorum. 17. Etsit

page.notes: The catchword "pulcri-" stands alone at lower right and is not repeated in the text. The "(go," at the end of the line "Quamuis & rimis est lacerata suis." is printed in the text; its sense is unclear (possibly a stray mark or abbreviation), so it is copied as printed. The verse lines of the epigram are set in italic type; the line-end hyphen "Ar-" is kept as printed. The page opens with a verse stanza that likely continues from the previous page. Reading of the italic verse is based on the scan and may contain small errors; no words were marked [?] because each was legible on inspection.
